scheme_name: Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Export Oriented Production: Large Cardamom Certified Nursery (Unit)
description:
The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing the export potential of spices, particularly large cardamom. 

This scheme was launched in 2018 under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote the export of spices by improving their quality and increasing production efficiency. 

The scheme specifically targets the cultivation of large cardamom, which is a high-value spice primarily grown in the northeastern states of India. 

The initiative aims to increase the production of large cardamom by 20 percent over the next five years. 

It also seeks to enhance the quality of cardamom to meet international standards, thereby increasing its competitiveness in global markets. 

The scheme focuses on establishing certified nurseries for large cardamom, which will provide high-quality planting material to farmers. 

Farmers are expected to benefit from this initiative through increased yields and better prices for their produce. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme includes a subsidy of up to 50 percent on the cost of establishing a certified nursery. 

This subsidy can amount to approximately INR 2.5 lakh per unit for setting up a nursery that can produce around 10,000 seedlings. 

The scheme also includes training programs for farmers on best practices in large cardamom cultivation. 

These training programs are conducted by the Spices Board of India in collaboration with state agricultural departments. 

Farmers participating in the scheme are also provided with access to quality planting materials, fertilizers, and pest management solutions. 

Eligibility for this scheme includes farmers who are engaged in the cultivation of large cardamom. 

Farmers must be registered with the local agricultural department to qualify for the benefits. 

There are no specific age limits for eligibility, but farmers must demonstrate a commitment to spice cultivation. 

Income criteria are not explicitly defined, but preference is given to small and marginal farmers. 

The application process for the scheme involves several steps. 

First, interested farmers must submit an application to the local agricultural office or the Spices Board. 

The application should include details such as land ownership documents and a proposed plan for the nursery. 

Farmers must also provide proof of their engagement in large cardamom cultivation. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by a committee formed by the Spices Board. 

If approved, farmers will receive a letter of sanction detailing the subsidy amount and conditions. 

The disbursement of funds typically occurs in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon the establishment of the nursery, while the second installment is provided after verification of the nursery's performance. 

The timeline for the entire process from application to fund disbursement can take up to six months. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Spices Board of India. 

The Spices Board operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and is responsible for the development and promotion of Indian spices. 

Farmers can contact the Spices Board through their regional offices for assistance and guidance. 

The contact details for the Spices Board include a toll-free number 1800 425 1660 and an email address at spicesboard@nic.in. 

The scheme also emphasizes research and development in cardamom cultivation. 

This includes the development of new high-yielding varieties of large cardamom. 

Research initiatives are aimed at improving disease resistance and enhancing flavor profiles. 

The scheme allocates a budget of INR 100 crore for the development of large cardamom over a five-year period. 

This budget is intended to cover various aspects of the scheme including nursery establishment, training, and research activities. 

The scheme also aims to create awareness about the health benefits of large cardamom. 

Large cardamom is known for its medicinal properties and is used in various culinary applications. 

The government plans to promote these benefits to increase domestic consumption alongside exports. 

In addition to large cardamom, the scheme also supports other spices such as black pepper and turmeric. 

The comprehensive approach aims to position India as a leading exporter of high-quality spices globally. 

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to enhance agricultural exports from India. 

The government aims to increase agricultural exports from USD 38 billion in 2020 to USD 60 billion by 2025. 

This initiative aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme also encourages the use of organic farming practices among large cardamom growers. 

Organic certification can significantly enhance the market value of large cardamom. 

Farmers are provided with training on organic farming techniques and pest management. 

The scheme also facilitates the establishment of farmer producer organizations. 

These organizations help farmers in collective marketing and negotiating better prices for their produce. 

The government is committed to ensuring that farmers receive fair compensation for their efforts. 

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in rural areas through increased production activities. 

It also aims to improve the livelihoods of farmers engaged in large cardamom cultivation. 

The success of this scheme will be monitored through regular assessments and feedback from farmers. 

The government plans to publish annual reports detailing the progress and impact of the scheme. 

This initiative represents a significant step towards sustainable agricultural development in India. 

The focus on export promotion and quality improvement is expected to yield long-term benefits for the spice industry. 

Farmers are encouraged to actively participate in this scheme to maximize their benefits. 

The government remains committed to supporting the spice sector through various initiatives and policies. 

Overall, the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom is a comprehensive effort to enhance the production and export of large cardamom in India.
